title: Conditional discourse
subtitle: Read a condition as a rhetorical move, not only a verb pattern.
overview: A condition may invite, warn, reassure, or reason from an assumed premise. Grammar marks the two clauses; the paragraph shows the rhetorical effect.
State the if-part and its conclusion first. Do not claim the author’s full implication from the conditional form alone.
